info.title: Fix fullscreen, badge swipe, copy button, shake

parts.text:
- Improve the fullscreen feature to fully cover the viewport as expected. This is useful for interactive previews of the user's sketch. The current implementation is not working as expected
- When you click on an achievement badge on the dashboard ,allow the user to swipe left/right to see the next/prev achievements whilst the popup is active. Current implement has improper layout and the swipe is not working. Also remove the "How to Earn" section from it
- On the symbol reference pages, add a copy-to-clipboard button (reuse the logic from the exercise view's code editor) . Currently pressing the copy icon crashes the app. Also use the copy icon on the exercise view code block 
- Restrict the shake festure to just allow the user to report errors on all other routes and keep the exercise options in the modal as is and reduce the sensitivity

Let me start by understanding the codebase structure. This is a learn-p5 Expo mobile app. The user has 4 feature requests:

1. Improve fullscreen feature to fully cover the viewport
2. Achievement badge popup: allow swipe left/right between achievements, fix layout, remove "How to Earn" section
3. Symbol reference pages: add copy-to-clipboard button (reuse logic from exercise view's code editor), currently copy icon crashes app. Use copy icon on exercise view code block
4. Restrict shake feature to just error reporting on all other routes, keep exercise options in modal as is, reduce sensitivity

Let me explore the codebase to understand the current implementations.

10: export function useShakeDetection(
11:   onShake: () => void,

13: ) {

17:   const onShakeRef = useRef(onShake);
18:   onShakeRef.current = onShake;
19: 
20:   const triggerShake = useCallback(() => {
21:     const now = Date.now();
22:     if (now - lastShakeRef.current < SHAKE_COOLDOWN_MS) return;
23:     lastShakeRef.current = now;
24:     if (haptic) {
25:       Haptics.impactAsync(Haptics.ImpactFeedbackStyle.Medium).catch(() => {});
26:     }
27:     onShakeRef.current();
28:   }, [haptic]);
29: 
30:   useEffect(() => {
31:     if (!enabled) return;
32: 
33:     Accelerometer.setUpdateInterval(UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS);
34: 
35:     const subscription = Accelerometer.addListener((accelerometerData) => {
36:       const { x, y, z } = accelerometerData;
37:       const history = historyRef.current;
38: 
39:       history.push({ x, y, z });
40:       if (history.length > WINDOW_SIZE) {
41:         history.shift();

50:       const magnitude = deltaX + deltaY + deltaZ;

52:       if (magnitude > SHAKE_THRESHOLD) {
53:         triggerShake();
54:       }
55:     });

59:       historyRef.current = [];

Now I understand the fullscreen implementation. The current fullscreen implementation:
1. In the WebView, clicking maximize button posts `toggleFullscreen` to RN and toggles `expanded` class on the sketch box (making it 400px tall).
2. In RN, the `toggleFullscreen` handler sets `fullscreen` state to true/false, which causes the WebView style to become `fullscreenWebView` (absolute, full size, zIndex 50), hides the header, breadcrumbs, keyboard, and shows a close button.

The user says "Improve the fullscreen feature to fully cover the viewport as expected... The current implementation is not working as expected."

Potential issues with current implementation:
1. The WebView is inside a container `View` with `flex:1`. When `fullscreen` is true, the WebView style is `position:absolute, top:0, left:0, width:100%, height:100%`. But `position: absolute` inside a flex container... The `styles.container` is the outer View with flex:1. When fullscreen, the header/breadcrumbs/kb are hidden, so the container is just the WebView. The absolute positioning should cover the full container. But the container itself is only as tall as its parent layout (below the app header / safe area?). The issue is that the container is a normal flex child of the screen layout; when fullscreen, the WebView with position absolute fills the container, not the whole viewport. If the container doesn't cover the full screen (e.g., it's within a navigator frame), the WebView won't cover the entire viewport.

Actually, a cleaner approach: when fullscreen, don't rely on absolute positioning. Just have the WebView take `flex:1` and the container naturally fill the screen since header etc. are hidden. But the issue is that the WebView's content (the HTML) still renders with the description, editor etc. The fullscreen should show ONLY the sketch preview covering the whole viewport. The current implementation just makes the WebView fullscreen but the HTML content still shows the description, editor, etc. - it's not really a preview-only fullscreen. Also the sketch-box height was only set to 400px in the WebView (the `expanded` class), not viewport-filling.

So "fully cover the viewport as expected" likely means: the sketch canvas should fill the entire viewport, and ideally the WebView itself covers the whole screen. Also there's the StatusBar hidden. There's also the issue that `scrollEnabled={!fullscreen}` disables scroll.

Let me think about how to best implement. Approach:
- When fullscreen is active, we want the WebView to cover the entire viewport (including under the status bar and any navigation area). Use React Native `Modal` with `fullScreen` presentation? Or absolute positioning with top/left/right/bottom = 0 and high zIndex. But RN absolute positioning is relative to parent. If the parent doesn't span the full screen, then it won't cover. The container view is the screen's root; in expo-router with a Stack navigator, the screen content is inside a header... but there might not be a header for this screen. Actually the screen has its own custom header. The Stack navigator's header is likely hidden for this route (since the app renders its own headers). Let me check the _layout files.

Also the WebView's internal content needs to show only the sketch, or scroll to the sketch, in fullscreen. Simplest robust approach:
- Use a `Modal` with `visible={fullscreen}` animationType="fade" (or none) and put a WebView inside that covers the whole screen. But the WebView with the whole exercise html is already mounted; we can't easily move it into a Modal. We could render a second WebView in the Modal for the preview. That duplicates p5 runtime cost.

Alternative: keep single WebView but when fullscreen, render it inside a full-screen Modal via React portal? Not straightforward in RN.

Better approach used commonly: wrap the WebView in a View that when fullscreen uses absolute fill within a container that is itself the full screen. Since header/breadcrumbs/keyboard are hidden when fullscreen, the container View with flex:1 will fill the screen (as the only child). Actually the container is the root View of the screen with `styles.container = {flex: 1}`. The root of the screen fills the screen (below the Stack header, if any). If the Stack header is hidden, it fills the full screen. So `position:absolute top:0 left:0 width:100% height:100%` should fill it.

Hmm, but there's a subtle issue: When `fullscreen` and WebView gets absolute style, the WebView still fills the same container. That should cover the full viewport as long as the container is full-screen. Why would it "not work as expected"? Possibly:
1. The `zIndex: 50` might not bring it above siblings within RN (it should within the same parent).
2. The absolute WebView with `width: 100%, height: 100%` — the WebView content is the full exercise page (description, preview, editor). The user sees the whole page scrolled, not just the sketch. They want the sketch to fully cover the viewport.
3. On iOS, `StatusBar hidden` plus safe area... The close button is at top 50.

Given the user description "This is useful for interactive previews of the user's sketch", the intent is: enter fullscreen → the sketch preview fills the entire screen for interactive play (the canvas is interactive - mouse/touch drawing). The current implementation does make the WebView fullscreen, but the HTML page inside still shows the description + editor sections, and the sketch-box is only 400px tall (expanded). So it's not a "full preview".

So the improvement: in fullscreen mode, the WebView should show a full-bleed sketch. Best approach:
- Send a message to the WebView when fullscreen toggles (e.g., `setFullscreen true/false`), and in the bridge, toggle a `body.fullscreen` class that hides description/editor/solution sections and makes `.sketch-box` fill 100vh/100vw.
- In RN, hide StatusBar, hide header etc. (already done), and make the WebView fill the screen. Keep the close button overlay in RN (already there). Also stop the keyboard from being shown.

That handles the "fully cover the viewport" on the content side.

Also, currently there's a bug: when toggling fullscreen, `setKeyboardVisible(false)` but when exiting, keyboard stays hidden — that's fine.

Let me also consider the WebView absolute positioning issue. When fullscreen, the WebView has `position: absolute` style with zIndex 50, and the close button is also absolute with zIndex 100. There could be an issue with the WebView not actually covering because parent has `pointerEvents`? Not really. I think the main fix is content-side full-bleed.

Also possibly the issue: on Android, `position: absolute` WebView plus hardware acceleration / zIndex can glitch. Using Modal for fullscreen would be more reliable. But moving a WebView into a Modal is possible: we can render the WebView inside a Modal and set the container to only render the WebView when not fullscreen, and render a Modal containing the WebView when fullscreen. But React re-mounts the WebView when moved between trees → loses state (editor content). The bridge posts code changes back to RN state, so we could restore the code. A robust alternative that avoids re-mounting: keep the WebView in place but make the root container full-screen when fullscreen. Actually the root container IS full-screen (it's the screen's root). So absolute positioning works if... hmm.

There's no existing "report error" flow. So I'll need to create one. The natural approach: a "Report Error" action in the ShakeModal on all non-exercise routes that opens the email client via `mailto:` with app version + route info pre-filled, OR opens a web URL (GitHub issues). Since this app seems to be self-contained, a `mailto:` link is the most straightforward "report errors" mechanism. 

Let me check the settings page for any existing support/feedback links to match conventions. Let me search settings/index.tsx quickly. Also check if there's a "report" link to a GitHub repo.

Actually, let me focus. The plan should:

**Task 1: Fullscreen**
- Redesign so fullscreen truly covers the whole viewport:
  - Use a native `Modal` (`presentationStyle="fullScreen"`, `statusBarTranslucent`, hide StatusBar) containing a dedicated fullscreen preview WebView that loads a new lightweight fullscreen HTML (p5 sketch full-bleed 100vw×100vh, interactive), receiving the current code via setCode + runSketch messages.
  - Keep the main exercise WebView as-is.
  - On enter: post current code to preview WebView and run. On exit: close modal (sketch keeps running behind or is disposed).
  - Update exerciseHtml maximize button: on click, post `toggleFullscreen` (RN drives everything) — stop toggling `.expanded` in the WebView, or keep `.expanded` only for the "non-fullscreen expand" fallback. Simplest: maximize button just posts toggleFullscreen; RN shows the modal.
  - Alternatively simpler: single-WebView approach + root-level overlay suppression. But Modal is more robust for "fully cover viewport".

Actually wait — let me reconsider the single-WebView approach with content CSS, since adding a whole new WebView + preview HTML is more code. The problem with single-WebView: root-level SideDrawer (openEdge zIndex 30) and DrawerFab (zIndex 35) and StatusBar would overlay it. The Modal approach fixes all of these cleanly because native Modal renders above everything.

But there's a concern: creating a second p5 instance while the first one is running. That's fine — independent WebView processes.

I'll go with the Modal + dedicated fullscreen preview WebView. It's the most reliable way to "fully cover the viewport".

Design for fullscreen preview:
- New util `src/utils/editor/fullscreenPreviewHtml.ts` exporting `getFullscreenPreviewHtml(colorScheme, ctaColor)` — HTML with p5 source, black background, `#sketch` div filling `100vw`/`100vh`, plus script that listens for `setCode` + `runSketch` messages, and a `resizeSketch` handler that re-renders on resize (orientation change). Actually to reuse `renderSketch` logic, simpler: the preview page just appends the code as a `<script>` in body like exampleHtml does, but full-screen. But we need live code from RN state. So the RN side posts code; the preview page's bridge runs it.

Simpler alternative: reuse `getExampleHtml`-like inline approach — on each open, we could even build `source={{ html }}` from current code using a fullscreen variant and set it directly as `source`. Since the Modal WebView mounts fresh on each open, we can just construct the HTML with the current code inline (like exampleHtml), no message passing needed! On open: `getFullscreenPreviewHtml(state.code)` → WebView `source={{ html }}`. The sketch runs full-bleed and interactive. On close: modal unmounts, WebView destroyed.

That's clean — no bridge messaging, no second WebView persisting. `source` is set when modal opens. Canvas interactive (touch events). Add exit button overlay in RN.

Also need to handle sketch errors gracefully (render error message in the HTML) and `describe()`/caption irrelevant.

Edge: Some sketches use `createCanvas(w,h)` — the canvas will render at its intrinsic size, centered on black background. That's the expected p5 behavior; fullscreen preview just shows it on a black full-screen surface. Good enough. Actually, to make it "cover the viewport", we might scale the canvas to fit screen? p5 canvas is fixed. We can center it and allow it to be interactive. That matches typical p5 fullscreen preview (Processing-style). We'll keep the canvas at its own size but center, on full black.

Hmm, but "fully cover the viewport" — the SKETCH box covers the viewport, canvas centered within. I think that's the intent.

**Task 2: Achievement modal**
- Rewrite AchievementBadgeModal:
  - Fix layout: card width = page width = `Math.min(screenWidth - 48, 420)` consistently (also compute on tablet), so snap works on all devices.
  - Ensure swipe works reliably: use FlatList with correct `snapToInterval` (== pageWidth == item width == FlatList width) or `pagingEnabled` ScrollView. Keep dots + index sync.
  - Remove "How to Earn" (already removed — verify no leftover).
  - Also add prev/next chevron buttons? The user said "swipe left/right" — swipe is the requirement. Dots give visual affordance.
  - The dismiss Pressable should not block gestures: keep overlay Pressable but ensure card is above; that's already the case.
  - Guard: when `items.length === 0` show empty state (already).

**Task 3: Copy buttons**
- Ref page: fix the crash + add copy buttons on each example code block (and keep syntax copy). "reuse the logic from the exercise view's code editor": implement a WebView-based clipboard helper OR use expo-clipboard properly.
  - Decision needed: which copy approach. Let me plan to create `src/utils/clipboard.ts` that:
    - On native: imports expo-clipboard statically and calls `setStringAsync`.
    - On web: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with textarea fallback (mirroring exerciseHtml logic).
  - Actually "reuse the logic from the exercise view's code editor" might specifically mean the WebView `execCommand` approach. But we can't run execCommand in native RN. However, we CAN mount a tiny hidden WebView on the ref page whose job is to copy text via execCommand (like the exercise editor does), and post text to it. That's the most literal "reuse". But that's heavy.
  
  Given AGENTS.md says expo-clipboard is the intended dependency for the copy feature and is present, and the crash is reported, maybe the real fix is simpler: the current `require()` inside the async function might crash on web because `expo-clipboard`'s web build requires HTTPS. Let me handle both: use expo-clipboard on native, navigator.clipboard on web, wrapped in try/catch, plus a fallback hidden-textarea WebView if both fail.

  I'll ask the user? No — I think I can decide. The robust plan:
  - Create `src/utils/clipboard.ts`:
    - `export async function copyToClipboard(text: string): Promise<boolean>`
    - On web: try navigator.clipboard, fallback execCommand textarea.
    - On native: try expo-clipboard setStringAsync.
  - Use it on ref page for syntax + example code blocks.
  - Update exercise editor (exerciseHtml.ts) copy button to show a copy icon (inline SVG/unicode) + "Copy"/"Copied" text. That satisfies "use the copy icon on the exercise view code block".
  - Also the ref page copy buttons already exist for syntax; add copy buttons to each example code block (so users can copy example code). The user said "add a copy-to-clipboard button (reuse the logic...)" — maybe they mean add it (they consider it not present / broken). I'll add per-example copy buttons too.

- Exercise view: "Also use the copy icon on the exercise view code block" — update exerciseHtml.ts Copy button to include a copy icon glyph + text.

**Task 4: Shake**
- Reduce sensitivity: bump `SHAKE_THRESHOLD` from 3.5 → ~5.5, maybe cooldown 1200 → 1500ms.
- Exercise route: keep existing actions as-is.
- All other routes: shake → "Report Error" only modal. Add useShakeDetection to dashboard, settings, learn index, ref (change actions), tips, onboarding? "all other routes" — I'll add to the main app screens: ref (both list and detail), dashboard, learn index, settings. For onboarding, probably skip (it's a flow). Keep exercise as-is.
- Create a reusable "Report Error" action component/handler: a ShakeModal with actions [Report Error (primary, mailto with subject/body including version + route), Dismiss].
- Need mailto support: `Linking.openURL('mailto:...?subject=...&body=...')`. What email? There's no known email in repo. Let me search for any contact email. If none, ask the user for the report target (email vs GitHub issues URL). This is a decision point.

parts.text:
The grep accidentally matched p5Source.ts (it's huge). There's no mailto or GitHub repo in the app source. So there's no existing "report errors" target. I need to ask the user what the report target should be (email vs GitHub issues), OR default to a mailto with a placeholder. Let me ask.

Actually, let me reconsider: the user said "just allow the user to report errors" — I should ask how they want errors reported (mailto to which address? GitHub issues URL? web form?). This is a genuine unknown.

Let me also check the settings/index.tsx for any feedback section and to know where shake would be added. And check learn/index.tsx quickly for shake context. Actually I have enough. Let me also check the `SearchOverlay` for the long-press reference (the 0dff70c fix). Not relevant.

Let me also double check the current exercise view's shake modal content to confirm "keep as is" — yes: Get Hint, Reset Code, View Reference, Dismiss.

Now, let me look at the git history of the current HEAD (dc713a6) — version 0.7.5. And AGENTS.md release cadence says every push to main must bump version + tag. So the plan should include version bump as part of the change. Actually AGENTS.md says the workflow: edit → bump-version → commit → tag → push. Since I'm only planning (not implementing yet), I'll include version bump step.

Let me also verify how `useShakeDetection` is used and whether the shake modal is presented as `position: absolute` inside the screen (it is - ShakeModal overlay is absolute inset:0 zIndex:1000). Note: ShakeModal is NOT a Modal component — it's a plain absolute overlay inside the screen's root View. On the ref page, it's rendered inside a fragment with SymbolDetail (a View) — the ShakeModal overlay is absolute but its parent is the screen container from expo-router, so it fills the screen. OK.

For adding shake to dashboard/settings/learn, they're screens with a root View — we add ShakeModal + useShakeDetection there.

Now, one more thing: the shake "report error" modal should probably include app version and route. We can build the body with APP_VERSION from constants/Version. Let me check Version.ts. It has APP_VERSION. Good.

Now let me formulate clarifying questions for the user:

1. **Error reporting target** for the shake "Report Error" action: email (mailto:) — need an address; or GitHub issues URL; or both/other. I'll ask.

2. **Copy approach**: The ref page crash is with expo-clipboard. Options: (a) fix expo-clipboard usage via a shared clipboard util (native+web), (b) WebView-based clipboard bridge reusing exercise editor's execCommand logic. The user explicitly said "reuse the logic from the exercise view's code editor", which is the WebView execCommand approach. I could present this as the recommended approach. But I might just decide: implement a shared `copyToClipboard` util that tries WebView-bridge... Actually the cleanest that matches "reuse the logic from the exercise view's code editor": mount a small off-screen WebView on the ref page that receives text via postMessage and copies using the same `copyToClipboard` JS from exerciseHtml (navigator.clipboard/execCommand), replying 'copied'. Hmm, that's a bit heavy but literal.

   Alternatively, maybe the crash is because `require("expo-clipboard")` was added but the dev build doesn't have the native module, while the WebView execCommand approach works because it doesn't need any native module. That strongly supports the WebView-bridge approach as the reliable fix.

   I'll ask the user which approach they prefer, with the WebView-bridge (reuse exercise logic) as recommended. Actually, the user already told us the desired approach: "reuse the logic from the exercise view's code editor". So no need to ask — implement WebView-based copy. But I should still confirm the report-error target.

3. Maybe ask about fullscreen: whether they want canvas scaled to fill screen (stretched) or centered at original size on a black full-screen backdrop. p5 canvases are fixed size; scaling would distort? Stretching is unusual for p5. I'll center on full-screen black backdrop (standard). I could ask but I think center-on-black is the safe default. name: Build & Publish Release APK

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "*"

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          NPM_INSTALLED=false
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            echo "Attempt $i to install npm dependencies..."
            npm install && NPM_INSTALLED=true && echo "npm install succeeded" && break
            echo "npm install failed (attempt $i)"
            if [ $i -lt 3 ]; then sleep 10; fi
          done
          if [ "$NPM_INSTALLED" != "true" ]; then
            echo "Failed to install npm dependencies after 3 attempts"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Verify CodeMirror bundle
        run: |
          BUNDLE_FILE="src/utils/editor/codemirror-bundle.generated.ts"
          if [ ! -f "$BUNDLE_FILE" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: $BUNDLE_FILE not found"
            exit 1
          fi
          SIZE=$(wc -c < "$BUNDLE_FILE")
          if [ "$SIZE" -lt 100000 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: CodeMirror bundle is too small ($SIZE bytes, expected >= 100000)"
            echo "Regenerate with: npm run bundle-editor"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "CodeMirror bundle OK ($SIZE bytes)"

      - name: Generate course modules
        run: npm run build-courses

      - name: Verify course modules
        run: |
          COUNT=$(find src/data/courses -name "*.ts" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
          if [ "$COUNT" -lt 16 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: only $COUNT course .ts files generated (expected >= 16)"
            echo "Regenerate with: npm run build-courses"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Course modules OK ($COUNT files)"

      - name: Setup JDK
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 17

      - name: Setup Android SDK
        uses: android-actions/setup-android@v3

      - name: Install NDK
        run: |
          NDK_INSTALLED=false
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            echo "Attempt $i to install NDK 27.1.12297006..."
            yes | $ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager \
              --install "ndk;27.1.12297006" || { echo "SDK manager failed"; sleep 10; continue; }
            NDK_DIR="$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/ndk/27.1.12297006"
            if [ -d "$NDK_DIR" ]; then
              echo "NDK installed successfully at $NDK_DIR"
              NDK_INSTALLED=true
              break
            fi
            echo "NDK directory not found, retrying..."
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$NDK_INSTALLED" != "true" ]; then
            echo "Failed to install NDK after 3 attempts"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Prebuild native project
        run: |
          PREBUILT=false
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            echo "Attempt $i to prebuild native project..."
            npx expo prebuild --platform android --clean && PREBUILT=true && break
            echo "prebuild failed (attempt $i)"
            if [ $i -lt 3 ]; then sleep 10; fi
          done
          if [ "$PREBUILT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "Failed to prebuild native project after 3 attempts"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Configure ABI splits for per-architecture APKs
        run: |
          sed -i '/android {/a\
          \    splits {\
          \        abi {\
          \            enable true\
          \            reset()\
          \            include "arm64-v8a", "armeabi-v7a"\
          \            universalApk false\
          \        }\
          \    }' android/app/build.gradle

      - name: Build release APKs (per ABI)
        run: cd android && ./gradlew assembleRelease

      - name: List split APKs
        run: find android -name "*.apk" -type f

      - name: Rename APKs to learn-p5-{tag}-{arch}-debug.apk
        run: |
          for apk in android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/*.apk; do
            dir=$(dirname "$apk")
            base=$(basename "$apk")
            arch=$(echo "$base" | sed -n 's/.*\(arm64-v8a\|armeabi-v7a\).*/\1/p')
            [ -z "$arch" ] && arch=universal
            mv "$apk" "$dir/learn-p5-${{ github.ref_name }}-$arch-debug.apk"
          done

      - name: Upload split APKs to release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/*.apk

#!/bin/sh
set -e

# Usage: ./scripts/bump-version.sh <version>
# Example: ./scripts/bump-version.sh 0.6.56
#
# Updates version in:
#   - app.json (expo.version)
#   - package.json (version)

VERSION="$1"

if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <version>"
  echo "Example: $0 0.6.56"
  exit 1
fi

# Validate version format (semver-like: X.Y.Z)
if ! echo "$VERSION" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; then
  echo "Error: Version must be in semver format (e.g., 0.6.56)"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Bumping version to $VERSION..."

# Update app.json
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const app = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('app.json', 'utf8'));
app.expo.version = '$VERSION';
fs.writeFileSync('app.json', JSON.stringify(app, null, 2) + '\n');
console.log('  Updated app.json');
"

# Update package.json
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json', 'utf8'));
pkg.version = '$VERSION';
fs.writeFileSync('package.json', JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + '\n');
console.log('  Updated package.json');
"

echo "Version bumped to $VERSION"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-push git hook (see AGENTS.md "Release cadence").
# Refuses a push to main unless the pushed commit range includes a version bump
# in package.json AND a matching vX.Y.Z tag exists locally.
#
# Reads stdin: <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha> per line.

set -e

while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
  # Only enforce on the main branch.
  if [[ "$local_ref" != "refs/heads/main" ]]; then
    continue
  fi

  # Resolve the range of commits being pushed.
  if [[ -z "$remote_sha" || "$remote_sha" == "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]]; then
    range="$local_sha"
  else
    range="$remote_sha..$local_sha"
  fi

  repo_dir="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

  # Detect a version bump in package.json within the pushed range.
  bumped_version=""
  if git diff --name-only "$range" -- "$repo_dir/package.json" 2>/dev/null | grep -q package.json; then
    bumped_version=$(git show "$local_sha:package.json" 2>/dev/null | node -e "
      let data='';
      process.stdin.on('data',c=>data+=c);
      process.stdin.on('end',()=>{
        try { process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(data).version || ''); }
        catch(e) { process.stdout.write(''); }
      });
    ")
  fi

  if [[ -z "$bumped_version" ]]; then
    echo "[pre-push] ERROR: push to main must include a version bump in package.json." >&2
    echo "           Run: sh scripts/bump-version.sh <X.Y.Z>  then commit, then:" >&2
    echo "           git tag vX.Y.Z  before pushing." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  # Confirm the matching tag exists locally.
  if ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$bumped_version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[pre-push] ERROR: package.json is at $bumped_version but tag v$bumped_version does not exist locally." >&2
    echo "           Run: git tag v$bumped_version  before pushing." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

exit 0

>

An offline first mobile app to help users learn p5.js through small (bite sized 🍣) exercises. It is not a replacement for the p5 web editor which has far more comprehensive editing features.

This is a [GSoC 2026](https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/programs/2026/projects/wmrV9qBT) project for the [Processing Foundation](https://processingfoundation.org).

## What is this ?

Learn P5 is a mobile app to help users learn how p5.js symbols (functions, classes, built-in variables) work by showing users their sketch preview during the exercise. It is not a replacement for the p5 web editor which has far more comprehensive editing features.

This is a [GSoC 2026](https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/programs/2026/projects/wmrV9qBT) project for the [Processing Foundation](https://processingfoundation.org).

## Who is this for ?

This app is intended for anyone who wants to learn p5.js at a relaxed pace that covers how each symbol works on the go, even without an internet connection to load resources such as the reference or web editor.

## How can I try it out ?

The app is currently available on Android only and ChromeOS if you are on the `dev` branch.

You can [grab the latest release here](https://github.com/skchr/learn-p5/releases/tag/latest)

## Where can I see and share suggestions ?

There's a few GitHub Discussions that are open to suggestions and where we post feature previews (screenshots and the like).

More threads will be created as the project progresses:

- After editing any `.yaml`, re-run `npm run build-courses` before type-checking or starting the app.

## p5.js bundling (always latest)

- `scripts/bundle-p5.mjs` queries the npm registry for the latest `p5` release, downloads `lib/p5.min.js`, and regenerates `src/utils/p5Source.ts` (the vendored minified source as `const _p = [...]; export const p5Source = _p.join("")`) plus `src/utils/p5Version.ts` (`export const p5Version = "X.Y.Z"`).
- `bundle-p5` runs first in `postinstall` (before `gen-reference`) and first in `npm start`, so the app always bundles the newest p5.js. `scripts/generate-reference.mjs` reads the version stamp from `src/utils/p5Version.ts` instead of hardcoding it.
- **`src/utils/p5Source.ts` and `src/utils/p5Version.ts` are gitignored build artifacts** — never commit them. A fresh clone regenerates them on `npm install`.

## Release cadence

- **Every push to `main` must bump the app version and create a matching git tag.** This is enforced by a `pre-push` git hook (`scripts/hooks/pre-push`, repo tracks `core.hooksPath = scripts/hooks`).
- To bump atomically, run `sh scripts/bump-version.sh <X.Y.Z>` — it updates `app.json` (`expo.version`) and `package.json` (`version`) together.
- Workflow: edit → `sh scripts/bump-version.sh 0.6.10X` → `git add -A` → `git commit -m "v0.6.10X: <subject>"` → `git tag vX.Y.Z` → `git push origin main && git push origin vX.Y.Z`.
- Patch bumps (`0.6.10X`) for bug fixes / small UX changes; minor bumps (`0.7.0`) for new features; major bumps for breaking changes. The hook refuses a `main` push if the pushed commit range doesn't include a version bump in `package.json` or if the matching `vX.Y.Z` tag doesn't exist locally.

## Loop Engineering

This repo uses loop engineering patterns. See:
- `.opencode/STATE.md` — current loop memory
- `.opencode/LOOP.md` — active loops and cadence
- `.opencode/loop-budget.md` — token caps
- `.opencode/loop-constraints.md` — binding agent rules
- `.opencode/loop-run-log.md` — run history
- `.opencode/gate.yaml` — path denylist + auto-merge allowlist
- `.opencode/skills/` — triage and verifier skills

Verify changes: `opencode run "Verify diff in worktree" --agent verifier`
